beats.text: The Spanish flu did not start in Spain.
beats.note: CBC says the exact origin is difficult to pinpoint, but it did not start in Spain.

beats.text: Spain's newspapers were free to report it.
beats.note: Spain stayed neutral in the First World War and faced no wartime censorship, says Science Friday. Madrid's ABC reported a strange illness on 22 May 1918.

beats.name: King Alfonso XIII
beats.role: Fell sick a week after people collapsed in the street, according to Science Friday.

beats.text: Elsewhere, the news was played down.
beats.note: CBC says officials in other countries chose to suppress the news or downplay how severe the virus was.
Science Friday lists China, the American Midwest and France as the suggestions. New America says it is still not agreed.

beats.context: At least 50 million people died worldwide, according to Science Friday and CBC. New America gives a broad range of 50 million to 100 million.

beats.text: It was named for the press that reported it, not for where it began.
